messages.text: Genge eager for England to build on victory in All Blacks rematch

metadata.summary: Ellis Genge called on England to back up their record victory over New Zealand as they go in search of an unprecedented hat-trick against the All Blacks.
metadata.content: Ellis Genge calls on England to follow New Zealand victory with another win over All Blacks in Nations Championship | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ellis Genge calls on England to follow New Zealand victory with another win over All Blacks in Nations Championship England thrashed New Zealand 37-12 at the Allianz Stadium on Saturday and will face each other again on Saturday, having both finished second in their respective Nations Championship groups; England also beat New Zealand last November Sunday 22 November 2026 17:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' James Cole breaks down how England achieved their record 37-12 Nations Championship win over the New Zealand Ellis Genge called on England to back up their record victory over New Zealand as they go in search of an unprecedented hat-trick against the All Blacks. The rivals face an immediate rematch of England's 37-12 procession at Allianz Stadium that meant they each finished second in their Nations Championship pools, setting up the battle for third place on Saturday. Following on from last November's 33-19 triumph , it was only the second time in the fixture's 121-year existence that England had registered consecutive wins - and Steve Borthwick's men are aiming to carve out their own piece of history. messages.text: Final Demand battles back to win Punchestown thriller

metadata.summary: Final Demand emerged best of the army of returning Willie Mullins stars on show after a thrilling finish to the John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase.
metadata.content: Punchestown: Final Demand battles back to win thrilling John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Punchestown: Final Demand battles back to win thrilling John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase In a John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase dominated by Willie Mullins-trained runners, Final Demand showed real determination to fend off last year's runner up Fact To File Sunday 22 November 2026 16:04, UK Image: Final Demand and Fact To File jump the final fence in the John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase Final Demand emerged best of the army of returning Willie Mullins stars on show after a thrilling finish to the John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase. With Henry de Bromhead's mare The Big Westerner a non-runner due to unsuitable ground, the champion trainer saddled each of the nine remaining runners, with last year's winner and subsequent Cheltenham Gold Cup hero Gaelic Warrior the 10/11 favourite in the hands of Paul Townend. Kitzbuhel and Daniel King took the field along for much of the two-and-a-half-mile journey, closely pursued by 8/1 shot Final Demand and Patrick Mullins, with Fact To File and Gaelic Warrior next in line. With the latter unable to quicken sufficiently to get himself into a challenge position, it was the 2024 winner and last year's runner-up Fact To File who looked most likely to prevail when taking over the lead on the run-in, but Final Demand battled bravely to get back up by a neck. messages.text: Verstappen wins wild Las Vegas GP as Ferraris collide again

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen produced a remarkable drive to win a wild Las Vegas Grand Prix that saw him withstand extreme pressure from George Russell and Kimi Antonelli before a late Mercedes collapse.
metadata.content: Las Vegas GP: Max Verstappen wins wild race as Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collide again | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Las Vegas GP: Max Verstappen wins wild race as Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collide again Max Verstappen wins wild Las Vegas Grand Prix; Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri claim double podium for McLaren after late Mercedes collapse saw George Russell and Kimi Antonelli drop back; Charles Leclerc penalised for causing collision with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton Sunday 22 November 2026 05:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Max Verstappen produced a remarkable drive to win a wild Las Vegas Grand Prix that saw him withstand extreme pressure from George Russell and Kimi Antonelli before a late Mercedes collapse. Pole-sitter Verstappen retained the lead at the start but the enormous power of a slipstream on the long straights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit made it impossible for the Dutchman to pull clear, and resulted in 34 changes of the lead and well over 300 total overtakes in the 50-lap race. First Russell, and then later newly crowned world champion Antonelli were each able to pass Verstappen on multiple occasions but the Red Bull driver calmly retook the lead within a few corners every time, expertly managing the deployment of his power.
